claims.note: Title and description kept identical to the current rendered version; the selection's generic 'comparable sandbox use cases' H1 was rejected because no CTR or query-level evidence supported replacing terms the URL already ranks for.
Vocabulary mapping (pause vs stopped/paused/archived vs standby/archive) is stated by each vendor's own lifecycle page; no ranking or measurement implied.

Every cell of the comparison table restates a documented lifecycle statement from the four checked pages; the E2B runtime window is from the sandbox page, the filesystem-only pause mode from the persistence page ("To save only the filesystem - a lighter snapshot that reboots on resume"), the archive/standby split from Blaxel, class dependence from Daytona.

Quoted from https://docs.e2b.dev/sandbox/persistence: pause saves both filesystem and memory by default, mode: 'filesystem' saves only the filesystem and reboots on resume; paused sandboxes kept with no automatic deletion; 24h Pro / 1h Hobby continuous window; timeout can auto-pause (settable to mode: filesystem); pause resets the window. The paragraph's 'lighter snapshot / slower resume' wording is corroborated on the linked page https://docs.e2b.dev/sandbox/filesystem-only-snapshots ('Expect the boot to take several seconds'; a full snapshot 'can serve again immediately'). All checked 2026-10-28 by the reviewer. This block corrects an earlier draft that denied the filesystem-only mode.

Standby transition ~15s, indefinite standby, under-25ms resume, 15-minute idle WebSocket/TCP timeout, archive semantics (no memory preserved, processes restarted) and standby billing statements all come from https://docs.blaxel.ai/Sandboxes/Overview checked 2026-10-28. The earlier 'not forkable' clause was removed in this revision per the prior review; the live Archived-mode section does state 'an archive only ever restores the sandbox it was taken from', so the removal was a scope choice, not a correction of an unsupported sentence. The current text asserts only the archive semantics quoted above.

The under-25ms figure is labelled as a vendor claim with no published workload, image size or region on the page; the article explicitly refuses to treat it as a cold start or as comparable to other providers.

Availability statement for the original fixture files in research/evidence/e2b-vs-daytona-vs-blaxel-2026/fixture; each file and its hash is recorded in receipt.public_artifacts, and the links point at the repository path. No performance claim.

Local offline run of the author's own fixture against transcribed vendor flags on 2026-10-28: exit 0, and a second invocation produced a byte-identical fit-report.json. 3 of 18 provider-class/profile pairs meet every documented requirement; all three are E2B / Pro, one per profile. The article states that the archive_filesystem_only flag means the archive lifecycle specifically, so a Daytona VM's documented filesystem-only snapshot does not satisfy it. Blaxel's standby-plus-archive option documents all three required flags but returns verify because no continuous-session limit is stated for the 6h profile. The run verifies the scorer's logic only, not any provider behaviour.
